change: the cyber practice hub links its five unit spokes, rebuilt against today's body rather than re-importing a stale sheet
_context: scripts/verify-cyber-practice-live.js reports 34 of 35 live checks passing.
The one failure is that ap-cybersecurity-practice links NONE of its five unit
spokes. The spokes serve 200, each reaches the course and its unit study page,
and every unit study page reaches its spoke. Only the hub's own downward edge
is missing, so those five pages are reachable from a study page and from
nowhere a student browsing the practice layer would look.
THE ROW ALREADY EXISTS, AND RE-IMPORTING IT WOULD HAVE COST MORE THAN IT FIXED.
imports/2026-09-04/cyber-practice-hub-links-pages.csv carries that handle with
all five links, and the other row in the same two row file matches its live
body character for character, so one row landed and one did not. Diffing the
stale row against today's live body finds three differences, not one:
insert  883 chars   the related-links CSS          expected
insert  643 chars   the five spoke anchors         expected
DELETE  722 chars   a Question of the Day block    NOT EXPECTED
The live page has GAINED a Question of the Day card since that sheet was
written: 152 questions across all five units. A MERGE republishes the whole
Body HTML, so re-importing would have silently erased it, and nothing about
re-running the file would have said so. The block is rebuilt from today's body
through the same lib/link-block.js instead.
The lesson is not about this sheet. A generated sheet is only valid against the
body it was generated from, and a live page can change under it between
generation and import. Check before re-importing anything more than a few hours
old, and check by DIFFING rather than by asking whether it looks current.

checks.name: the repair, and the proof the stale sheet was destructive
checks.expect: OK - 22 checks, 5 mutations, every one caught by the rule that claims it

checks.name: the practice package it belongs to did not regress
checks.expect: OK - 29 checks, 16 mutations, every one caught by the rule that claims it

checks.name: lib/link-block.js is shared, and its other consumer suite still passes
checks._why: There is no dedicated link-block suite; the module is exercised through its consumers. smoke:cyberpractice above is one and smoke:linkgraph is the other, and this pass calls build() and check() exactly as they do.

checks.name: a second implementation proves nothing was deleted, by diff rather than by marker list
checks._why: The generator proves 'nothing was lost' against a list of markers it declares, and a list cannot report that it has stopped covering the page: same shape as the stale-count patterns that let two wrong numbers onto the practice exam earlier today. This is Python, shares no code, and requires that EVERY character of the live body survives and every difference is an insertion. It also re-derives the finding itself, that the sheet already in imports/2026-09-04 deletes a 722 character Question of the Day block.
checks.expect: OK - 20 checks re-derived from the sheet by diff, independently of the generator

checks.name: the sheet clears the Matrixify preflight
THE ONE THAT MATTERS: let the build drop a section the live page had
checks._why: This is the stale sheet's defect, reproduced. The guard compares each declared marker on the live body against the built body and refuses when one is lost. Without it the generator happily writes a sheet that deletes live content, which is precisely what imports/2026-09-04 would have done.
checks.expect_failure: MUTATION: dropping the carried marker from the output is refused

checks.name: accept a partial edge instead of insisting on all five spokes
checks._why: A sheet that adds three of five links reads as a fix and leaves two pages orphaned. The count is derived from the spec rather than typed, and the assertion is what makes the derivation load-bearing.
checks.expect_failure: MUTATION: a spec with three spokes instead of five is refused

checks.name: stop refusing a missing stored body
checks._why: An empty Body HTML cell in a MERGE erases the live page. This is the most expensive mistake available in this whole pipeline and the refusal has to be proven, not assumed.
checks.expect_failure: MUTATION: a missing stored body is refused, never an empty cell

checks.name: the practice hub reaches all five spokes, and lost nothing doing it
checks._why: This is the existing package verifier and it is failing on exactly this edge today: 34 passed, 1 failed, the failure naming all five missing spoke handles. That single check flipping is the whole deploy. Its 34 other assertions are what prove the import cost nothing, including that the hub still carries its FRQ and labs sections.

not_covered: WHY the row did not land the first time. The other row in the same file did, so this was not a whole-file refusal. Matrixify's own import log would say, and nobody has it. The practical answer is the same either way: re-check the live body before re-importing, and the generator now does.
Whether the Question of the Day block should be on the practice hub at all. It is, somebody put it there deliberately, and this pass is not the place to second-guess it.
The five spokes are still linked from only two places once this lands: their unit study page and now the hub. Whether they deserve an entry in the nav is a separate question and a theme change.
